items.title: Leslie Gourse interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: I heard Symphony Sid on the radio every night from midnight to five AM

ctx.x: Now you’ve written for magazines and a couple of well known books, Louis’ Children and of course the book about Joe which we’ll talk about more, but what brought you into the field of jazz?

Well I always listened to jazz, you know, as a teenager and in high school in Providence, Rhode Island, I used to go to a place called the Celebrity Club when I was under age and shouldn’t have been there. And then when I came to New York I just gravitated towards listening to it. I heard Symphony Sid on the radio every night from midnight to five AM, and I used to go to the jazz clubs. And why I liked jazz more than any other music I don’t know. I did like other music too. I liked pop, I liked rock & roll, I…
There’s something about seeing it live, you know, in a club, where it’s so spontaneous and you kind of catch that moment. It’s really fascinating.
